name: GO Classes 2024 | Weekly Quiz 21 | Asymptotic Notation and Loop Time Complexity

question.text:
Consider $\text{Iterated logarithm}$ of $n,$ written $\log^\ast n$ (usually read "$\log$ star $n$"), is the number of times the logarithm (base $2$) function must be iteratively applied before the result is less than or equal to $1.$
Mathematically,
$$\lg ^{*} N=\min \{k \mid \underbrace{\lg \lg \cdots \lg }_{k} N \leq 1\}$$
For example-
$\begin{aligned} \lg ^{*} 2 &=1,\\
\lg ^{*} 4 &=2,\\
\lg ^{*} 16 &=3,\\
\lg ^{*} 65536 &=4,\\
\lg ^{*}\left(2^{65536}\right) &=5 \end{aligned}$

Which of the following is/are correct about the implementation of $\log \ast n?$

In all options, $\log()$ is a function which calculates $\log$ base $2$ of a given number.

  1.  
    int iteratedLog(double n)
{
    if (n > 1.0) {
        return 1 + iteratedLog( log(n));
    }
    else return 0;
}
  2.  
    int iteratedLog(double n)
{
    int count=0;
    while (n > 1.0) {
        n = log(n);
        count++;
    }
    return count;
}
  3. $\log \ast n=\left\{\begin{array}{clc}0 & \text { if } & n \leq 1\\
    1+\log \ast(\log n) & \text { if } & n>1\end{array}\right.$

     
  4. $\log ^{*} 2^{m}=1+\log ^{*} m$ for $m>1$

What is the time complexity of the code given?

int i = 1, j = 2;
while (i <= n) {
    sum += 1;
    i = i * j;
    j = j * 2;
}
  1. $\Theta(n)$
  2. $\Theta(\sqrt{\log n})$
  3. $\Theta\left(n^{2}\right)$
  4. $\Theta\left((\log n)^{2}\right)$

Rank the following functions by increasing order of growth; that is, find an arrangement $g_{1}, g_{2}, g_{3}, g_{4}$ of the functions satisfying $g_{1}=O\left(g_{2}\right), g_{2}=O\left(g_{3}\right), g_{3}=O\left(g_{4}\right). ($For example, the correct ordering of $n^{2}, n^{4}, n, n^{3}$ is $n, n^{2}, n^{3}, n^{4})$
$$
f_{1}=(n !)^{1 / n} \quad f_{2}=\log n^{n} \quad f_{3}=n^{n^{1 / 2}} \quad f_{4}=n \log n \log \log n
$$

  1. $f 1, f 2, f 3, f 4$
  2. $f 3, f 2, f 4, f 1$
  3. $f 1, f 2, f 4, f 3$
  4. $f 2, f 4, f 1, f 3$

What is the time complexity of the code given?

for (i = n; i > 0; i--) {
    for (j = 1; j < n; j = j * 2) {
        for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
            printf("hi");
        }
    }
}
  1. $\Theta(n)$
  2. $\Theta\left(n^{2}\right)$
  3. $\Theta\left(n^{3}\right)$
  4. $\Theta\left(n^{2} \log n\right)$

Let $f(n)=\Omega(n), g(n)=O(n)$ and $h(n)=\Theta(n)$. Then $[f(n) . g(n)]+h(n)$ is:

  1. $\Omega(\mathrm{n})$
  2. $O(n)$
  3. $\theta(n)$
  4. None of these

Which of the following statement is FALSE?

  1. If $f(n)=\mathcal{O}(g(n))$ and $f(n)=\Omega(g(n))$, then we have $(f(n))^{2}= \Theta\left((g(n))^{2}\right)$
  2. If $f(n)=\mathcal{O}(g(n))$ and $f(n)=\Omega(g(n))$, then we have $f(n)=g(n)$
  3. $2^{n}+n^{2}=\mathcal{O}\left(3^{n}\right)$
  4. $2^{n}+n^{2}=\mathcal{O}\left(2^{n}\right)$

Rank the following functions by increasing order of growth. That is, find any arrangement $g 1, g 2, g 3, g 4$ of the functions satisfying $g 1=O(g 2), g 2=O(g 3), g 3=$ $\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g} 4)$.
$$
\begin{aligned}
&f_{1}(n)=2^{(\log n)^{4}}
&f_{2}(n)=\pi^{n}
&f_{3}(n)=n^{5(\log n)^{2}}
&f_{4}(n)=\sqrt{2^{\sqrt{n}}}
\end{aligned}
$$

  1. $f 1, f 3, f 4, f 2$
  2. $f 3, f 1, f 4, f 2$
  3. $f 1, f 3, f 2, f 4$
  4. $f 1, f 3, f 4, f 2$

Which of the following statement is/are FALSE? Assume that $\log$ base is $2$ in all options.

  1. $8^{\log \left(n^{2}\right)} \in \Theta\left(n^{6}\right)$
  2. If $f, g$, and $h$ are functions from the natural numbers to the non-negative real numbers with $f(n) \geq g(n) \forall n \geq 1, f(n) \in \Theta(h(n))$, and $g(n) \in \Theta(h(n))$, then $(f(n)-g(n)) \in \Theta(h(n))$
  3. $(\log n)^{a}$ is $\mathrm{O}\left(n^{ b}\right)$ for any constant $a$, and for any constant $b>0$
  4. $T(n) = O(f(n))$ and $g(n)$ is a function whose value is never negative then $g(n) T(n)$ is $O(g(n) f(n))$

Consider two statements $\text{S1}$ and $\text{S2}$ below.

  • $\text{S1}: $ If $f_{1}(n)=O\left(g_{1}(n)\right)$ and $f_{2}(n)=O\left(g_{2}(n)\right)$, then $f_{1}(n)+f_{2}(n)=O\left(\max \left\{g_{1}(n), g_{2}(n)\right\}\right)$.
  • $\text{S2}:$ If $f_{1}(n)=\Omega\left(g_{1}(n)\right)$ and $f_{2}(n)=\Omega\left(g_{2}(n)\right)$, then $f_{1}(n)+f_{2}(n)=\Omega\left(\min \left\{g_{1}(n), g_{2}(n)\right\}\right)$.

Which of the following is correct?

  1. $\text{S1}$ is true but $\mathrm{S} 2$ is false
  2. $\text{S}1$ is false but $\text{S}2$ is true
  3. Both statements are true
  4. Both statements are false

Arrange the following functions in their increasing order of growth.

$\left(\begin{array}{c}
\text { If f(n) = O(g(n) and g(n) = O(h((n)) then order is f(n), g(n), h(n).} 
\end{array}\right)$

In all options $\log^{2}n$ means $(\log n)^{2}$

  1. $2^{\log ^{2} n}, \qquad 4^{\log n},\qquad(\sqrt{2})^{\log n},\qquad 5 \sqrt{n}$
  2. $4^{\log n},\qquad 2^{\log ^{2} n},\qquad 5 \sqrt{n},\qquad(\sqrt{2})^{\log n}$
  3. $5 \sqrt{n},\qquad(\sqrt{2})^{\log n},\qquad 4^{\log n},\qquad 2^{\log ^{2} n}$
  4. $5 \sqrt{n},\qquad 4^{\log n},\qquad 2^{\log ^{2} n},\qquad(\sqrt{2})^{\log n}$

What will be the time complexity of $\text{fun()}?$

int fun(int n) {
    int count = 0;
    for (int i = n; i > 0; i /= 2)
        for (int j = 0; j < i; j++)
            count += 1;
    return count;
}
  1. $\Theta(n)$
  2. $\Theta(n \log n)$
  3. $\Theta\left(n^{2}\right)$
  4. $\Theta\left((\log n)^{2}\right)$

What will be the time complexity of following pseudo code?

s=1
while s <= (log n)*(log n)
    s=3*s;
  1. $\Theta\left((\log n)^{2}\right)$
  2. $\Theta(\log n)$
  3. $\Theta (\log \log n)$
  4. $\Theta (\log \log \log n)$

Suppose

  • $\text{A}=(\log\ n)^{k}$
  • $\text{B}=n^{\epsilon}$

Assume that $k \geq 1$ and $\epsilon>0$

What is the relation $\text{between}$ the asymptotic time complexities of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}?$

  1. $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{B})$
  2. $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{o}(\mathrm{B})$
  3. $\mathrm{A}=\Omega(B)$
  4. $\mathrm{A}=\omega(B)$

What is the time complexity of the code given?

for(i=1;i<=n;i++)
    for(j=1;j<=n;j=j+i)
        printf("GO Classes");
  1. $\Theta\left(n^{2}\right)$
  2. $\Theta( n \log n )$
  3. $\Theta (n \log \log n)$
  4. None of these

Consider Iterated logarithm of $n$, written log ${ }^{\star} n$. Defined as below.
$$\lg ^{*} N=\min \{k \mid \underbrace{\lg \lg \cdots \lg }_{k} N \leq 1\}$$
Which of the following is TRUE?

(log base can be considered as any constant)

  1. $\lg \lg { }^{*} n=o\left(\lg ^{*} \lg n\right)$ here o is small oh
  2. $\lg ^{*} \lg n=o\left(\lg \lg ^{*} n\right)$ here $o$ is small oh
  3. $\lg ^{*} \lg n=\boldsymbol{\Theta}\left(\lg \lg { }^{*} n\right)$
  4. $\lg ^{\star} \lg n$ and $\lg \lg ^{\ast} n$ are not comparable
